chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about whether the people of the religions (Ahl al-Kitab) are to be made to swear an oath, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not make them swear except by Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمِلَلِ: People of the religions (specifically Ahl al-Kitab/People of the Book)
key_terms.إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ: Except by Allah (exclusive condition for the oath)
key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفُونَ: To be made to swear an oath (passive verb)

ai.seo_question: How should non-Muslims be made to swear an oath in Islamic courts according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the judicial procedure for administering oaths to Ahl al-Kitab, emphasizing the universality of Allah's name over specific religious identifiers. It reflects the Shia scholarly principle of maintaining theological consistency in legal proceedings by avoiding references to entities that might imply polytheism or distinct divine attributes in the eyes of the non-Muslims. This ruling ensures that the oath remains binding and recognizable across different monotheistic traditions while adhering to Islamic monotheism.
